judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Three Performance Objectives under the same Topic '4. Division' (same rank 2). The first objective is dividing whole numbers not exceeding 48 by 2-6 without remainder; the second is expressing whole numbers not exceeding 48 as products of factors. Finding and expressing factors of a number depends on the ability to divide it exactly (without remainder), so proficiency in the division objective substantively supports success in the factorization objective, consistent with the source ordering (objective 1 then objective 2) within the same table row. This justifies a permitted developmental direction rather than mere co-topic reinforcement. Shared LC tags/text overlap (division, whole numbers) and page proximity are consideration triggers, not the basis for the verdict.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Two Performance Objectives under the same Theme (MENSURATION AND GEOMETRY) and Sub-Theme (Shapes). The first concerns identifying the 'square corner' of a 2-dimensional shape (Topic 2, Two dimensional shapes); the second concerns identifying and counting the flat faces of a cube and cuboid (Topic 1, Three dimensional shapes). These are complementary shape-property identification skills — corners of 2D shapes and flat faces of 3D solids (whose faces are themselves 2D shapes) — giving substantive conceptual coherence within the Shapes strand. However, they sit at the same grade rank in distinct parallel topics with no evidence that proficiency in one is developmentally required for or supports success in the other, so a directional buildsTowards is not warranted. Token/trigram overlap is dominated by boilerplate ('pupils should be able to') and generic words, not conceptual dependency.

judgment.rationale: Both are Performance Objectives under the same Topic '2. Subtraction' (Theme/Sub-Theme Basic Operations, Grade PRIMARY THREE, same rank 2). Second SFI ('subtract 2-digit numbers with exchanging or renaming', listed as objective 1) is whole-number subtraction fluency, while first SFI ('subtract fractions with the same denominator', objective 4) applies subtraction to numerators of like fractions. Proficiency in whole-number subtraction with renaming substantively supports success in subtracting like fractions, and the source objective sequencing (1 before 4) corroborates this developmental direction, warranting buildsTowards from the whole-number objective (second) to the fraction objective (first). Same-rank direction rests on this conceptual foundation plus source ordering, not on shared hierarchy alone.
